# Motrix v1.8.19 fixtures

These fixtures were generated by the **actual bundled aria2 1.36.0 executable**
from the official Motrix `v1.8.19` Git tree. The generator extracts that binary
from Git and verifies its SHA-256 before executing it. It does not use the
current Motrix engine, an adjacent engine checkout, or a real user profile.
The binary itself is not checked in.

Run on macOS arm64 from the repository root:

```sh
node tests/fixtures/legacy-v1/generate.mjs
```

The local checkout must contain tag `v1.8.19`, commit
`a0a1fe90f7e9f6d305ed2b512f62c8d36c2fb95a`. The authoritative binary is
`extra/darwin/arm64/engine/aria2c`, Git object
`f4a274061acbbc22c6eb1ab487ffdc0e80ad1b71`, SHA-256
`1527c4d071c16c1266880e93750e385cdd4e9d2a950d7f56cb5a21125e3bd311`.
Source reference: [official Motrix v1.8.19 tree](https://github.com/agalwood/Motrix/tree/v1.8.19).

The generator creates a disposable profile and a separate downloads directory,
as normal installations do. Only loopback HTTP/RPC/tracker endpoints are used;
DHT, PEX and local peer discovery are disabled. The HTTP response is generated
test data, and the two-file private torrent describes generated test data.
No private tokens, trackers, credentials or user paths are included.

`download.session`, both `.aria2` files and the saved RPC `.torrent` are actual
old-engine output. The `.aria2` and `.torrent` bytes are unmodified.
`partial.bin.gz` contains the actual partial HTTP output, compressed
without changing its uncompressed bytes. Profile/download directory prefixes
and the HTTP port in text files use placeholders. The saved torrent contains
its original loopback tracker port. Ports, incomplete block boundaries and
torrent filenames can vary on regeneration; `provenance.json` records the
resulting digests and the source binary identity.

`user.json` and `system.json` are **source-derived defaults**, evaluated from
the tagged `ConfigManager.js` with disposable paths and an English locale.
They are not presented as output from running the complete old Electron app.
The engine is launched using these defaults and the tagged `aria2.conf`, with
the documented loopback/isolation overrides in the generator.

The saved RPC torrent filename is the SHA-1 of its complete metadata bytes,
which differs from its info hash. Its session reference is outside the profile
grant. Scanner tests deliberately verify that this real layout yields an
unselectable `metadata-required` row rather than reading arbitrary downloads
paths from `system.json`. A separately labeled test variant copies metadata
inside the grant to verify parsing and file selection. The external-directory
case still needs an explicit additional user grant before it can be imported.

These fixtures prove compatibility with this tagged binary's serialization;
they do not prove packaged cross-platform migration, historical HTTP validator
availability, or safe continuation from arbitrary legacy files.
